title: Po memory that forgets on purpose: refresh-free ephemeral pages
idea: Po: 'memory that forgets on purpose.' Extracted: the OS and compiler tag pages whose data will be overwritten or discarded within the retention window (AI activations, KV-cache chunks, network buffers) as ephemeral; the controller skips refresh on those rows and stores an expiry timestamp so a late read faults instead of returning corrupt data.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, 16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth at 32-64 Gb): on AI servers where much of DRAM holds short-lived tensors, refresh energy and bandwidth loss on those rows go to zero.

title: Microwave oven: single-wafer microwave annealers replace quartz-tube furnaces
idea: Stimulus 'microwave oven' (heats the food, not the plate) -> a 10-person team builds 2.45/5.8 GHz single-wafer microwave annealers that activate dopants and crystallize dielectrics at 400-500 C by coupling to carriers and dipoles, avoiding batch quartz furnaces.
why: Cuts anneal energy several-fold, removes high-purity quartz tube consumption, and the lower thermal budget admits abundant low-melting metals (Al, Cu) into DRAM.

title: 2T1C cell with in-cell preamp shrinks capacitor to 1 fF stub
idea: Box [1 fF stub cap, AR ~12:1 | Si access + stacked vertical oxide-TFT read transistor | current sense | monolithic | CZ Si | standard]: the storage node both holds charge on a short capacitor and gates a stacked read transistor, so readout is non-destructive current rather than charge sharing.
why: Capacitor charge wall and materials: AR 70:1 drops to ~12:1, cutting mold-etch fluorocarbons and ALD precursor per bit ~5x and removing destructive-read write-back energy.

title: Eliminate binary storage: three bits per gain cell
idea: Store 8 charge levels on a gain cell's storage node, whose read current maps monotonically to node voltage; read with a column-shared 3-bit SAR ADC and write with a precision DAC plus write-verify.
why: Silicon, water, energy and quartz per bit fall ~2-3x for the same wafer starts.

title: Multi-beam electron writing for DRAM's critical layers
idea: Inverts 'critical layers must be printed by EUV from one supplier': use ~100k-beam electron direct write with silicon field-emitter tip arrays and blanking apertures, dedicated to DRAM's highly repetitive cell layers where pattern data compresses to a small repeat unit.
why: Removes EUV (single supplier, tin source) and masks for 5-7 layers; array regularity makes throughput tractable; target ~3x lower capital per critical layer.

title: Ship the mask defect: unrepaired, pellicle-free reticles
idea: Reverse mask qualification: use EUV/DUV reticles with residual blank defects and no pellicle; every repeating print defect lands at the same cell address in every die, which goes into a single mask-level defect table loaded into each die's remap ECC.
why: Cuts mask cost and turnaround and removes scarce EUV pellicles; repeating defects are known erasures, cheap to correct within the 1% budget.

title: Two bits per cell: multi-level DRAM with 1% level errors
idea: Rearrange the cell's voltage range into four charge levels sensed by a successive-approximation sense amp, accepting ~1% level misreads corrected by Gray-coded symbol ECC.
why: Halves wafers, crucibles, helium and tungsten per bit (~2x density) at a modest periphery cost.

title: Eliminate the 8-kilobit page: activate only 512-bit wordline slivers
idea: Split each master wordline into 16 locally gated segments with per-segment sub-wordline drivers so an activate charges only the 512 bitlines that hold the requested burst.
why: Attacks the 128x overfetch (fact 8): ~5.9 pJ per useful bit falls to ~0.4 pJ, >10x per random access, and fewer aggressor rows for row hammer.

title: Bit-year embodied-resource labels reward memory that lives longer
idea: Time-scale shift from purchase to service life: require DIMM and HBM vendors to publish helium, tungsten, water and energy per bit-year of rated service. Tie procurement and tax credits to the lowest per-bit-year figure, rewarding 10-year-rated modules and take-back programs.
why: Most DRAM retires at 3-5 years while the silicon is good for 15+. Doubling service life halves chokepoint-material intensity per delivered bit-year.

title: Nanoimprint template also prints the self-assembly guide pattern
idea: Combine nanoimprint and directed self-assembly: one imprint stamps sparse 40-80 nm guide posts plus a chemically patterned brush, then a high-chi block copolymer fills in 4-8x denser features and heals imprint defects for capacitor-hole and active arrays.
why: Replaces 2-3 EUV/ArF multi-patterning layers with an imprint tool ~1/10 the cost of an EUV scanner, cutting single-supplier dependence and ~1 MW/tool energy.

title: Fab consortium pre-buys helium from small U.S. wells
idea: Within $1M/24 months: form a buyers' consortium that signs 10-year forward offtake with small helium developers in Kansas, Montana and Wyoming, using the $1M for diligence, legal setup and escrow seed while member fabs supply the volume commitment.
why: Small helium projects stall for lack of offtake; guaranteed demand unlocks new domestic supply and removes Qatar exposure.

title: Solid-state 213 nm laser steppers replace neon-buffered ArF excimers
idea: Box [standard | standard | standard | standard | Si | DUV projection lithography with fifth-harmonic diode-pumped Nd:YAG (213 nm) source]: generate DUV in CLBO/KBBF nonlinear crystals instead of an Ar/F2/Ne gas discharge, and re-coat 193 nm-class optics for 213 nm.
why: Neon (about half once came from Ukraine) and krypton/fluorine gas logistics: zero rare-gas consumables and longer source life; reaching ~100 W average power is the hurdle.

title: Mirror-silvering bath grows rutile capacitor dielectric at 80 C
idea: Tollens' silver-mirror chemistry coats any shape from solution; adapt chemical bath deposition of Al/Nb-co-doped rutile TiO2 (k ~80-100) from aqueous titanium peroxo complexes onto a rutile-templating MoO2 electrode, filling 70:1 holes by diffusion instead of vacuum ALD.
why: Reaching k ~70+ breaks the capacitor charge wall without raising aspect ratio, using abundant titanium and molybdenum instead of hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium, in an atmospheric bath with far less energy and precursor waste.

title: Ice cube tray: freeze crystallization reclaims fab rinse water
idea: Stimulus 'ice cube tray' (ice freezes out pure and rejects solutes) -> run RO reject and spent rinse water through an indirect-contact freeze crystallizer; pure ice crystals are washed and melted back into the UPW feed while brine concentrates for zero liquid discharge. Latent heat is 334 J/g versus 2,260 J/g for evaporation.
why: Water intensity: lifts fab water recovery from ~60-80% to >95% at ~1/5 the energy of thermal evaporators, opening water-stressed U.S. sites.

title: Substitute harvested second-life DRAM for newly fabricated bits
idea: Industrialize take-back of retired server DIMMs: robotic desoldering, at-speed retest with per-row retention profiling, and re-binning into CXL memory-expander cards for tier-2 memory, with controller ECC and adaptive refresh hiding weak cells.
why: A reused bit needs essentially zero fab water versus ~0.3-1 L per new Gb, a >100x cut per delivered bit, and it adds usable supply immediately during the shortage.

title: Porous-silicon lift-off wafers reuse one CZ parent fifty times
idea: Box [standard cell | Si access | voltage SA | thin device film bonded to handle | 30-50 um epi film | anodize + epi + bond + cleave]: anodize a double-porosity release layer on a premium CZ parent, grow device-grade epi from trichlorosilane, bond to a low-grade handle and cleave at the porous layer, then re-anodize the parent and repeat.
why: High-purity quartz crucibles (Spruce Pine >80%) and polysilicon: one CZ slice yields ~50 DRAM substrates, cutting HPQ crucible and poly consumption per wafer by roughly 10-30x.

title: PCB-free all-silicon memory module as a two-material recycling stream
idea: Worsen: mount DRAM on brominated FR-4 boards full of glass fiber, copper and gold that are costly to separate. Flip: build memory modules on a silicon or glass-core interposer card with only Cu and Al metallization, so the whole module is a two-material recycling stream and the chips can be re-bonded.
why: Recyclability and scarce-resource intensity: removes brominated flame retardants and Au finishes and shortens the signal path, which saves I/O energy.

title: Top dummy die etched into a water microchannel cold plate
idea: Combine HBM's topmost dummy spacer die with a cold plate: deep-etch 100 um microchannels into it and pump water/glycol through, replacing two-phase immersion in fluorinated (Novec-type, being phased out) fluids for hot AI racks.
why: Removes PFAS coolants; ~20 C lower HBM junction temperature roughly halves retention leakage, so refresh rate and its 16-33% idle power share halve.

title: Homesteader builds upward: memory-layer foundry on legacy logic wafers
idea: Persona: a homesteader who adds a floor instead of buying land. A U.S. business deposits non-volatile BEOL memory layers, such as nitride ferroelectric or MRAM below 400 C, directly on customers' finished logic wafers in existing lines.
why: Needs no extra crucible-grown silicon, no EUV and no helium-cooled high-AR etch. Puts memory next to compute (fact 5).

title: Po no fab owns a whole chip: relay-fab consortium of 200mm sites
idea: Po: 'no fab makes a whole chip.' Extracted: split the 180 nm DRAM flow into modules (front-end transistors, capacitor module, metallization, test) assigned to under-used U.S. 200 mm analog and MEMS fabs, moving wafers between them in sealed carriers under a shared copy-exact spec and a pooled tooling fund.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: uses existing idle capacity instead of a $15B greenfield fab, with time to first supply measured in months.

title: Soviet core-memory veteran shrinks ferrite cores into nanorings
idea: Persona: a Soviet engineer who ran ferrite-core computers, now working at 40 nm. Permalloy (Ni80Fe20) nanorings threaded by a vertical copper via store a bit as a clockwise or counterclockwise flux-closure vortex. Current pulses through the via write the bit, and a small TMR sensor on a notch in the ring reads it.
why: Non-volatile with core-memory endurance. Flux closure has no stray field, so rings pack densely. Uses only abundant Ni, Fe and Cu, with no Pt, Co or Ir.

title: Smoke detector: hydrogen-tracer sniffers replace helium leak detectors
idea: Stimulus 'smoke detector' (a cheap solid-state sniffer) -> a 10-person team builds Pd-alloy thin-film hydrogen sniffer leak detectors that use non-flammable 5% H2/95% N2 forming gas as tracer for gas lines, chambers and packages instead of helium mass-spectrometer detection.
why: Removes helium from routine leak testing, a top fab helium use, at ~1/5 the tool cost.

title: Print to the edge: sell the wafer rim as high-BER dies
idea: Reverse the edge exclusion: pattern and keep dies out to ~1 mm from the wafer edge, where uniformity is worst, and sell the rim dies with raw BER up to 1% under stronger ECC.
why: Adds ~6-10% more dies per wafer from the same silicon, crucible, helium and tool time; a near-free supply increase.

title: Shift legacy DRAM orders onto 200 mm mature lines
idea: Market-scale shift: DDR3, LPDDR2 and low-density (<=2 Gb) DRAM for industrial, automotive and IoT still occupy 300 mm leading DRAM lines. Requalifying them on existing 200 mm 40-90 nm DRAM and specialty fabs lets leading lines convert those starts to DDR5/HBM.
why: Frees several percent of leading-edge DRAM starts for AI-class parts with zero new fabs, using mature lines that have spare capacity.

title: Po wafers have no back: double-sided arrays on one wafer
idea: Po: 'the wafer has no back side.' Extracted: double-side-polish 200 mm wafers, build transistors and capacitors on the front, flip and build a second array on the back with a low-temperature capacitor module last, and connect the faces at die edges for power and I/O.
why: Silicon, crucible quartz and wafer starts per bit halved: one wafer carries two arrays at 180 nm, lowering substrate and some tool costs per bit.

title: MAPPER's bankrupt multibeam e-beam reborn as DRAM tile character projection
idea: MAPPER Lithography (13,000 beamlets, bankrupt 2018) died on throughput for random logic. DRAM arrays are ~95% identical cells: give each beamlet a stencil aperture of a full 8x8-cell tile so one flash writes 64 cells, exposing fluorine-free metal-oxide or HSQ resist.
why: Displaces EUV (one supplier, ~1 MW per tool, tin plasma, hydrogen) on 5-7 critical array layers at ~1/5 the capex; PFAS photoacid generators eliminated; 64x flash multiplication brings throughput to production class.

title: Substitute thermophoretic particle shielding for after-the-fact wafer cleaning
idea: Hold wafers a few kelvin above ambient on heated carriers and stages and add biased electrostatic guard grids, so thermophoretic and electric forces repel sub-100 nm particles before they land, then skip cleans whose only job is particle removal.
why: Prevention instead of washing removes much of the particle-clean step count, cutting that water >10x; the same physics already protects EUV reticles.

title: Cold memory: nitrogen-cooled racks make leaky abundant cells work
idea: Reverse the temperature assumption: run DRAM-class arrays at 77 K in liquid-nitrogen racks (N2 is abundant, unlike helium), where leakage falls by orders of magnitude, so small capacitors with simple Al2O3/SiO2 dielectrics hold charge.
why: Removes the need for high-k ZrO2/HfO2 and tall capacitors; retention rises ~10^3-10^4x, cutting refresh energy and capacitor process steps.

title: Light as memory: silica fiber recirculating delay loops
idea: Inverts 'memory stores data at rest in matter': store bits as optical pulses circulating in a ~10-20 m silica fiber or silicon-nitride spiral loop with semiconductor-optical-amplifier regeneration, giving 50-100 ns worst-case access to 0.1-1 Mbit per loop at 1-10 Tb/s with WDM, a modern mercury delay line.
why: Built from the most abundant material (silica), with no capacitor, no DRAM fab, no tungsten; serves streaming buffers such as packet queues and KV-cache rings.

title: Iodine-loaded fluorine-free chemically amplified EUV resist
idea: Periodic-table walk, I (53): build resists from iodinated phenolic polymers with iodonium/sulfonium photoacid generators carrying non-fluorinated anions (camphorsulfonate, carboxylates); iodine's high EUV cross-section and secondary electrons make up for the weaker acid.
why: Removes PFAS photoacids; ~2-3x higher photon absorption lowers dose, raising wafers per hour on the single-supplier EUV tool.

title: Deep-UV photochemical activation forms oxide dielectrics at 150 C
idea: Effect: photolysis. 185/254 nm UV breaks sol-gel ligands and makes ozone and atomic oxygen in situ, condensing dense M-O-M networks of AlOx and ZrOx from spin-coated or inkjet precursors at <=150 C. This replaces furnace and ALD steps for storage-node and gate dielectrics in stacked tiers.
why: Energy and vacuum-tool capital; removes the thermal budget that drives quartz furnace consumables; printable dielectrics cut capital intensity for oxide memory tiers.

title: Eliminate the 1 V array: 0.25 V storage with auto-zeroed sense amps
idea: Store and sense at 0.25 V from an efficient buck rail and run all long data wires at 50-100 mV, using offset-cancelling sense amps that sample their own offset onto a capacitor before each activate.
why: Bitline and data-line CV2 drop ~16x; the 4x lower field across the capacitor lets thin Al2O3/TiO2 stacks replace Hf/Zr high-k.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers from dopant-contrast silicon superlattices
idea: Instead of Si/SiGe stacks (germanium is ~60%+ China-controlled), grow alternating p++ boron-doped and intrinsic Si tiers in one low-temperature epi run. Anodization porosifies only the p++ layers, which are then oxidized into tier isolation. Scale shift: atom-level dopant contrast replaces alloy contrast to define 26+ tiers.
why: Removes germanium supply risk and the Si/SiGe critical-thickness strain limit on tier count, potentially allowing 50+ lattice-matched tiers for 3D DRAM.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers by doping-selective electrochemical etch
idea: Periodic-table walk, P (15): grow a 30-100-tier all-silicon superlattice of n+ (P) and p (B) layers instead of Si/SiGe, then remove the p layers laterally in TMAH under electrochemical bias, where the n layers passivate at the p-n junction.
why: Avoids export-controlled Ge; an unstrained homo-Si stack can pass 100 tiers with no HF/CF4 lateral recess (fact 2).

title: Batik dopant-resist stacks make germanium-free 3D DRAM tiers
idea: In batik, wax marks what the dye must not touch; grow an all-silicon stack in which sacrificial tiers are heavily boron-doped and channel tiers lightly doped, then remove the sacrificial tiers laterally with a dopant-selective electrochemical or HNA-type etch, replacing SiGe sacrificial layers.
why: Eliminates germanium (China ~60%, export-controlled) and SiGe lattice strain that caps tier count, enabling 30+ tiers from domestically made silane and diborane.

title: Gold-free, glass-cloth-free DRAM packaging via fan-out redistribution
idea: Ideal: a package that is just the chip. Closest: replace board-on-chip gold-wire FBGA packages on BT laminate (near-monopoly T-glass cloth) with wafer-level fan-out: copper RDL plated directly over a reconstituted mold wafer, solder balls on the RDL.
why: Removes gold wire and BT/T-glass substrate chokepoints, shortens I/O paths (lower pJ/bit), ~20-30% lower package cost per GB.

title: Supercritical CO2 replaces ultrapure water in cleaning
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero ultrapure water for post-etch clean and dry. Run residue removal and drying in supercritical CO2 with small co-solvent and chelator doses inside sealed cluster modules, recompressing and recycling >95% of the CO2.
why: UPW use (~2-4 m3 per wafer) can fall up to ~50%; with no liquid meniscus tall capacitor pillars do not collapse, which allows higher AR; fabs in water-stressed U.S. sites become permittable.

title: Substitute dry plasma abatement and sorbents for wet exhaust scrubbers
idea: Replace burn-wet point-of-use abatement with atmospheric microwave plasma that decomposes PFCs and NF3, followed by regenerable dry Ca(OH)2/CaO beds that capture HF and F2 as calcium fluoride for resale.
why: Wet scrubbers need continuous water streams; dry abatement cuts scrubber water >10x and closes a fluorine loop that offsets the fluorspar chokepoint.

title: Closed fluorine loop: scrubber fluorspar back to on-site F2
idea: Periodic-table walk, F (9): capture HF and fluorocarbon exhaust in Ca(OH)2 scrubbers as synthetic CaF2, convert it back to HF, and electrolyze KF.2HF on-site to F2 for chamber cleans, replacing NF3.
why: Removes NF3 (GWP 17,200, few suppliers) and virgin fluorspar (China/Mexico) dependence; F2 has GWP 0.

title: Vitrimer mold compound lets packages reflow open for die harvest
idea: Worsen: encapsulate dies in thermoset epoxy that can only be burned or acid-dissolved. Flip: mold with a silica-filled vitrimer whose exchangeable covalent bonds soften at ~200 C, so packages can be reflowed open, dies lifted out intact and the compound remolded.
why: Die reuse and package material recovery: intact known-good dies could be re-packaged at a fraction of the cost of new silicon.

title: Calculator-style chip-on-board DIMMs skip the package substrate
idea: Cheap calculators and LED boards bond bare dies straight to the board under a glob-top; mount known-good DRAM dies directly on the module PCB with copper-pillar flip-chip and one over-mold per module, eliminating per-die BT substrates, glass cloth and individual mold caps.
why: Package substrates and low-CTE glass cloth are a separate Japan-concentrated chokepoint; removing them cuts materials and package cost per GB ~10-20% and shortens traces for lower I/O energy.

title: At-tool electrochemical synthesis of ALD precursors from bulk metal
idea: Worsen: rely on a handful of overseas suppliers for TEMAZ, TDMAT and other organometallic precursors shipped in hazardous cylinders. Flip: put a small electrochemical cell at each ALD tool that anodically dissolves Zr, Ti or Al metal into ligand solution, making precursor on demand at the purity the tool needs.
why: Precursor chokepoint and shipping hazards: ~2-3x lower precursor cost and less inventory, from commodity metals.

title: Silicon-on-nothing cavities under storage nodes cut 125 C leakage
idea: Magnify vacuum as the insulator: anneal patterned trench arrays in hydrogen so silicon surface migration seals empty cavities beneath each storage junction, giving SOI-like isolation on a bulk wafer.
why: Removes junction area under the node, so leakage at 125 C drops ~5-10x, and avoids SOI's two-wafer bonding, which doubles silicon and quartz per wafer.

title: Mussel-catechol temporary bonding tape for HBM wafer thinning
idea: Mussels stick underwater with catechol (DOPA) proteins that let go when oxidized. Coat roll-to-roll a dopamine-functional polymer tape that bonds device wafers to carriers for thinning and TSV reveal, then debonds at room temperature in a mild oxidizing or pH-switch rinse.
why: Replaces costly specialty and fluorinated temporary adhesives and laser-debond tools in HBM stacking, trimming the TSV tax and raising thin-wafer yield.

title: Kombucha: bioleaching vats recover metals from scrapped memory modules
idea: Stimulus 'kombucha SCOBY' (a living culture doing chemistry in a jar) -> a 10-person team runs Acidithiobacillus and cyanogenic Chromobacterium bioleaching vats on shredded DIMMs and memory boards, recovering gold, palladium, copper and tantalum at ambient temperature.
why: Turns e-waste into domestic strategic metals without smelters, feeding tantalum and gold back into memory packaging and targets.

title: Saltatory wordlines: Ranvier-node repeaters let abundant conductors replace tungsten
idea: Like myelinated axons that regenerate the signal at nodes of Ranvier, split each buried wordline into short segments, each with a tiny regenerating driver placed every 64-128 cells in a CMOS-under-array layer. Short segments tolerate 5-10x higher sheet resistance, so TiN, doped polysilicon or Mo-silicide can replace the tungsten fill.
why: Cuts tungsten demand (China ~80%) in buried wordlines and removes WF6 fluorine chemistry; also shortens wordline RC. The cost is a little extra under-array periphery.

title: Langmuir-assembled silica-sphere monolayers replace array lithography masks
idea: Ideal: a mask that assembles itself on water. Closest: self-assemble a close-packed monolayer of 40-60 nm Stober silica spheres on a Langmuir trough, transfer it to wafer or panel, shrink the spheres by O2/ion trimming, and use it as a hexagonal hard mask for capacitor-node or vertical-channel arrays; only coarse periphery uses conventional litho.
why: 100x: hexagonal DRAM arrays match a sphere lattice, so a cent of TEOS-derived spheres replaces an EUV exposure; with cheap multi-tier stacks array patterning cost per GB drops >100x. Trades grain-boundary defects needing spare rows and defect-tolerant mapping.

title: Aluminum-doped zinc oxide top plate replaces germanium SiGe fill
idea: Combine the plate electrode and pillar-forest gap fill (zero added masks, same plate mask): replace the boron-doped poly-SiGe plate fill over the TiN top electrode with ALD/CVD ZnO:Al, which fills conformally at ~200 C and conducts ~1e-3 ohm-cm.
why: Removes germanium (China-dominated, export-controlled) and GeH4 from every DRAM wafer; low temperature protects the dielectric.

title: Nitrogen-cooled racks freeze leakage, switching refresh off
idea: Inverts 'memory runs at room temperature': immerse DRAM modules in liquid nitrogen from air-separation units (no helium), where junction and subthreshold leakage fall by >1e6 and retention stretches from 64 ms to hours or days; firmware disables refresh for working sets whose lifetime is below the cryogenic retention.
why: Zero refresh power and bandwidth, wire resistance falls ~5x; nitrogen is the most abundant gas and LN2 costs cents per liter.

title: Canon nanoimprint for DRAM: repair maps absorb defects, fluorine-free resist
idea: Nanoimprint stalled on particle-induced defects and template wear. DRAM already repairs defects with spare rows and columns: imprint capacitor-hole and storage-node layers in UV-cure acrylate resist with a non-fluorinated siloxane release layer, map imprint defects by fast inline e-beam inspection, fuse them to redundancy, and replicate cheap daughter templates from one e-beam master.
why: Replaces EUV or SAQP on 2-3 array layers; imprint uses ~1/10 the energy and capex of EUV; resist and release chemistry are PFAS-free; ~10-15% wafer cost cut.

title: Vertical charge-coupled strings store 64 bits per pillar without capacitors
idea: A bit is just a charge packet and needs only a potential well, not a capacitor plus transistor. Use NAND-like vertical pillars whose tiered gates clock 3-phase wells that shift packets to one sense amplifier at the pillar top: 192 tiers give 64 bits per pillar at 60 nm pitch.
why: ~56 nm2/bit (~15x today) with one contact per 64 bits; deletes per-cell capacitor dielectric (Zr/Hf), tungsten contacts and EUV. Transfer inefficiency and serial latency are the risks.

title: 2050 engineer drives MRAM with orbital currents in titanium
idea: Persona: a 2050 engineer who sees heavy-metal spin-Hall layers as a detour. Write SOT-MRAM with the orbital Hall effect of the light metals Ti and Cr, converting orbital current to torque through a 1 nm Ni insertion layer. The beta-W, Pt and Ta underlayers disappear.
why: Non-volatile SOT-MRAM without tungsten (China ~80%) or Pt. Low-resistivity Ti also cuts write energy.

title: Orbital Hall torque from titanium and oxidized copper, no heavy metals
idea: Effect: the orbital Hall effect makes orbital angular-momentum currents in light metals (Ti, Cr, Cu/CuOx) with Hall conductivity rivaling Pt spin Hall. A Ti or Cu/CuOx channel plus a thin Ni orbital-to-spin conversion layer switches an MTJ free layer, building SOT-MRAM working memory with no Pt, W or Ta.
why: Scarce-metal intensity (W China ~80%, Ta conflict mineral, Pt): SOT-MRAM gives ~1-5 ns, no refresh and >1e14 endurance; if orbital torque efficiency reaches ~0.5, switching current is ~3-5x lower than with W.

title: Bistable buckled silicon-nitride nanobeams as non-volatile DRAM cells
idea: Box [mechanical state of a pre-buckled 300 nm SiN beam | electrostatic pull-in hysteresis, self-selecting with no transistor | capacitive sense of up/down state | BEOL cavity array | Si | LPCVD SiN from DCS+NH3 + vapor-HF/ethanol release in N2]: snap a compressively stressed nanobeam between two stable states with a 10 ns pulse; GHz beam frequencies allow 5-20 ns switching and non-contact snapping avoids wear.
why: Materials: a cell built only from Si and N, with no high-k, W, Hf or oxide semiconductor, and no refresh; endurance and density are the open risks.

title: Cast-iron skillet seasoning: reusable silicon nitride crucibles for CZ
idea: A seasoned cast-iron pan lasts generations; make CZ crucibles from reaction-bonded silicon nitride (U.S. silicon powder nitrided in U.S. air-separated nitrogen) with a self-renewing Si3N4/SiO2 'seasoning' coat reapplied between pulls, so one crucible serves dozens of 300 mm pulls.
why: Removes dependence on the single Spruce Pine site and on foreign crucible fabricators while making crucibles reusable; nitrogen doping is already prized for vacancy-defect control, turning contamination into a feature.

title: Drop-in molybdenum precursor swap in existing tungsten CVD chambers
idea: Molecule-level substitution: replace WF6/H2 with fluorine-free MoO2Cl2 in the same CVD chamber hardware on existing trailing lines. Contacts and periphery lines fill with Mo, whose ~11 nm mean free path needs no TiN barrier at small widths.
why: Cuts tungsten (China ~80%) in contacts. Mo supply is diversified (U.S., Chile, Peru), and removing fluorine ends oxide attack.

title: Zinc-oxide/cuprous-oxide diodes enable eight-deck selector-capacitor crosspoint DRAM
idea: Retention only needs reverse leakage below ~1e-4 A/cm2 at a 400 nm2 cell (Q~5e-16 C over 64 ms), within reach of wide-gap oxide heterojunctions. Stack a ZnO/Cu2O diode on a small MIM capacitor at each 4F2 crosspoint, deposited below 300 C, 8 decks high.
why: 4F2 x 8 decks = ~12x density with no per-cell transistor, using only Zn, Cu, Al and O. Forward current for 10 ns writes and half-select disturb are the risks.

title: Rice cooker: rice-husk silica replaces rare-earth ceria in CMP
idea: Stimulus 'rice cooker' -> burn rice husks (~20% silica) under controlled conditions into amorphous nanosilica, then surface-dope with Fe, Mn or Ti to mimic ceria's chemical-tooth Si-O-metal bonding; use it as an oxide/nitride-selective STI and ILD CMP abrasive.
why: Ceria is a China-dominated rare earth; agricultural-waste abrasive removes it and lowers slurry cost, with U.S. rice-belt feedstock.

title: RF filter aluminum-boron-nitride ferroelectric in an endurance-shielded cell
idea: Phone BAW filters are sputtered aluminum nitride made in vast volume. Adapt boron-doped AlN (a ferroelectric wurtzite needing no Sc or Hf) as a ferroelectric-gated transistor bit on the same sputter tools, and shield its finite endurance with an SRAM write-back buffer that absorbs hot writes so each cell sees <1e9 cycles over its life.
why: A capacitor-free, Hf-free, Sc-free nonvolatile bit needs no refresh. The risks are the high coercive field (~4-6 MV/cm) and fatigue.

title: Eliminate transistor leakage: bistable SiC nano-relay memory cells
idea: Each cell is a ~100 nm electrostatically actuated SiC or TiN beam that snaps between two buckled stable states and closes a contact for a zero-leakage read; switching costs aJ of mechanical energy plus wiring.
why: Zero off-current removes refresh and the leakage tail, and the tiny switched charge makes access energy wire-limited, >10x below DRAM; contact endurance is the open risk.

title: Light-addressed photoconductive access through silicon-nitride waveguide wordlines
idea: Effect: photoconductivity. A PECVD SiN waveguide grid (300 C) replaces metal wordlines, and each cell's access device is a microcrystalline-Si photoconductor (PECVD 250 C). A laser pulse into one row's waveguide turns its photoconductors on (on/off ~1e5) while dark cells isolate their storage nodes.
why: Tungsten wordlines, wordline-driver periphery (fact 7) and row hammer (fact 9, since there is no electrical wordline coupling); all layers are BEOL-compatible.

title: Vertical-farming stacks memory tiers on logic, deleting separate wafers
idea: Vertical farms grow many crop tiers on one footprint. Adapt this by depositing 8-16 tiers of capacitor-free BEOL memory directly over the accelerator's logic die, replacing HBM's separate DRAM dies, base die and TSV stack.
why: HBM consumes ~3x the wafer area per bit plus 8-12 separate CZ wafers per stack. Monolithic tiers use no extra crystal or quartz crucible per bit and remove the TSV tax (Fact 6) and much of the data-movement energy (Fact 5).

title: Venus-flytrap bistable nanoshells: refresh-free mechanical bits, nanoimprinted
idea: The flytrap snaps between two stable curvatures using little energy. Nanoimprint arrays of 200 nm pre-stressed metallic-glass domes roll-to-roll on foil that snap between two stable states under a gate pulse; the state is read capacitively and holds with zero leakage.
why: No charge leakage means no refresh (16-33% of idle power) and no storage capacitor; NEMS at this scale can switch in ~10-100 ns, but fatigue endurance is the open risk.

title: Eliminate new silicon: harvest and re-certify DRAM from retired servers
idea: Run a reverse-logistics business that pulls DDR4/DDR5 modules from decommissioned hyperscale servers, retention-bins them hot, and redeploys them behind CXL memory expanders with stronger ECC as a second memory tier.
why: Each reused GB avoids new wafer starts, energy and water; could add several percent of global supply within months during the shortage.

title: Capacitor plate electrode doubles as an in-field annealing heater
idea: Combine the common top plate with a Joule heater: the one added mask cuts the plate into serpentine segments with two contacts each, so during idle maintenance the controller pulses a sub-array to ~150-200 C for seconds to anneal out variable-retention (VRT) trap cells.
why: Recovers retention-tail cells in service, extending module life and usable yield ~1.5-2x and reducing demand for scarce new bits.

title: Substitute subtractive-etched aluminum for plated copper damascene layers
idea: Form upper DRAM metal layers by sputtering Al-Cu and patterning with Cl2/BCl3 dry etch, then gap-fill with spin-on low-k, so no electroplating baths, CMP or post-CMP rinses are needed.
why: Plating plus CMP is a top BEOL water user; subtractive metal cuts that module's water >10x, and aluminum is abundant and US-smelted.

title: Po cleanroom the size of a wafer: sealed nitrogen tool tunnels
idea: Po: 'the cleanroom is no bigger than the wafer.' Extracted: drop ballroom ISO-class cleanrooms and connect tools with sealed, nitrogen-purged carrier tunnels and tool-mounted mini-environments, so only ~2% of the building volume is ultraclean and the rest uses ordinary industrial HVAC.
why: Energy and capital: cleanroom air handling is roughly 30-40% of fab electricity and the shell is a large share of the $15B+ capex; cutting ultraclean volume ~50x could halve facility energy and shrink building cost.

title: IBM MXT memory compression revived for KV caches with block-float codecs
idea: IBM's Memory eXpansion Technology (2000) compressed main memory ~2x but died on latency and poorly compressible general data. Put a fixed-ratio 2:1 codec for KV-cache and activation pages (shared-exponent block-float plus entropy coding) in the HBM base die or CXL controller, with fixed page frames so there is no fragmentation and decode is a few-ns pipeline.
why: AI tensors have low-entropy exponents; 1.5-2x effective capacity means 33-50% fewer DRAM wafers, and all their helium, quartz, tungsten and water, per served gigabyte.

title: Lighthouse: solid-state 213 nm interference lithography for cell arrays
idea: Stimulus 'lighthouse' (one coherent beam marks a whole coastline) -> pattern the perfectly periodic DRAM capacitor and active arrays by three-beam immersion interference from a 5th-harmonic Nd:YAG 213 nm laser (no neon excimer gas, no mask, no EUV), then pitch-split with self-aligned spacers.
why: Removes EUV single-supplier dependence, tin plasma and ~1 MW per-tool power, plus neon, for the array layers that dominate EUV count; tool cost ~10x lower.

title: Laser-polymer spalling slices ingots into wafers without kerf
idea: Combine subsurface IR laser modification with polymer stress spalling: a focused 1.3-2 um laser writes a damage plane 775 um deep, and a chilled polymer film bonded on top cracks the wafer off along it, replacing multi-wire sawing that turns ~40% of the ingot into kerf.
why: ~40-60% more wafers per ingot, so proportionally fewer quartz crucibles, less polysilicon energy and no saw slurry water.

title: Smart-valve rinse segregation feeds matched water regeneration trains
idea: Worsen: mix every rinse stream into one waste line so nothing can be reclaimed. Flip: install conductivity/TOC-sensing smart valves at each wet bench that split rinse water into ~5 contaminant classes, each piped to a matched regeneration train (EDI, UV-ozone, RO), reaching ~90% water reuse by design.
why: Water intensity: ~90% reuse versus ~40-60% typical, making fabs viable in water-stressed U.S. sites.

title: Chokepoint-aware process kit: element budgets as design rules
idea: Inverts 'choose materials for performance, then source them': annotate every process module with grams of W, Hf, Ru, He, PFAS, quartz and water per wafer plus a supplier-concentration (HHI) index, and run a flow optimizer that picks the recipe meeting electrical targets at minimum chokepoint exposure.
why: Makes scarce-resource intensity a first-class metric; expected 30-60% cut in chokepoint-weighted inputs per bit by surfacing substitutions (Al for W, Mo for Ru, H2 for He).

title: Vinyl record: electroless nickel-boron contact plugs replace CVD tungsten
idea: Stimulus 'vinyl record' (an electroformed nickel stamper copies every groove) -> fill bit-line and storage-node contacts bottom-up with electroless Ni-B or Ni-P plated from a self-catalyzing seed below 90 C, instead of WF6 CVD tungsten.
why: Removes WF6 (tungsten plus fluorine chemistry) and vacuum CVD tools from contact fill; plating baths are cheap and not supply-concentrated.

title: Zero-waste garment cutting reclaims wafer-edge area with tiny tiles
idea: Zero-waste fashion nests pattern pieces to use the whole bolt of cloth. Lay out capacitor-free memory as 1-2 mm2 self-contained tiles (own sense amps, redundancy and BIST) that fill the partial-die ring at the wafer edge, then sell them as chiplets binned by tile count.
why: Large DRAM dies waste ~6-10% of each wafer at the edge. Tiny capacitor-free tiles avoid the capacitor-height non-uniformity there and recover most of it, cutting crystal, quartz and energy per bit proportionally.

title: Wordline-last: aluminum replaces tungsten after all hot steps
idea: Inverts 'buried wordlines are formed early, so they must be refractory tungsten': form a sacrificial poly-Si/SiN buried wordline, finish capacitors and every >450 C anneal, then exhume the sacrificial line through a slot and refill it with high-pressure reflowed aluminum on a thin TiN barrier (replacement-metal-gate logic applied to the DRAM array).
why: Removes tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 from the wordline; Al in narrow trenches gives ~1.5-2x lower line resistance than W plus barrier, cutting wordline RC; aluminum is smelted in North America.

title: Hydrogen-cooled chucks borrowed from turbo-generator cooling
idea: Large power-plant generators are cooled with hydrogen because it conducts heat better than helium; use 1-20 Torr hydrogen as electrostatic-chuck backside gas in etch, CVD and implant tools, with sealed-band chucks, leak-rate interlocks and hydrogen from on-site electrolysis.
why: Backside cooling is the largest fab helium use, and Qatar's ~30% is offline; H2 thermal conductivity (~0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K for He) gives equal or better wafer temperature control at ~1% of helium cost, removing most fab helium demand.

title: Cartridge-based fab tools refurbished across node transitions
idea: Worsen: scrap or export whole fab tool sets at every node transition. Flip: build process tools as standard frames with swappable process cartridges and open control interfaces, so older DRAM fabs refurbish chambers for new chemistries (gain cells, 3D) instead of buying new tools.
why: Capital intensity and time to capacity: could cut new-node tool capex ~30-40%.

title: Fertilizer-plant fluorine: Florida phosphate byproduct replaces imported fluorspar
idea: Phosphate fertilizer plants scrub fluorosilicic acid from off-gas and mostly neutralize it; convert it via the bifluoride route to anhydrous HF and then to electronic-grade HF, NF3 and F2 at a Gulf Coast plant, recovering silica as a coproduct.
why: U.S. HF depends on imported fluorspar from Mexico and China; phosphate byproduct could supply all fab fluorine chemistry domestically while keeping it fluorocarbon-free.

title: ThruChip inductive coupling revived to strip signal TSVs from HBM
idea: Revive Kuroda's abandoned ThruChip Interface: replace the thousands of signal TSVs in an HBM stack with on-die spiral coils that couple data inductively between thinned dies, keeping only a few coarse, wide-pitch power TSVs.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): frees TSV keep-out area and copper fill and removes a major yield detractor; claims 1.5-2x more HBM bits per wafer.

title: Ruthenium-free strontium titanate capacitor stays paraelectric through 125 C
idea: Magnify k to ~150: grow SrTiO3 by ALD on TiN over a SrO/TiO2 nanolaminate seed instead of Ru/SrRuO3 electrodes. STO is a quantum paraelectric with no phase transition anywhere near 125 C.
why: Same charge at aspect ratio ~20 (fact 1), with no hafnium and no ruthenium; strontium and titanium are abundant (Sr from Spain and Mexico).

title: Crust-only DRAM built from Earth's most abundant elements
idea: Minify the bill of materials to Si, O, N, Al, Ti, C and H: polysilicon wordlines with 4x shorter subarrays, thermal ONO capacitors, aluminum interconnect with Al2O3 liners and TiN only as a barrier. No W, Mo, Hf, Zr, Ru, Co, Ta, In, Ga or Ge.
why: Every element is available domestically at ton scale and these are automotive-proven 125 C materials, so no single-country export ban can stop production.

title: Candle stub: cold-spray refills eroded sputter targets
idea: Stimulus 'candle stub' (melt leftovers into a new candle) -> a 10-person team cold-sprays fresh Ti, Ta or W powder into the erosion racetrack of spent sputter targets, then HIP-densifies and re-machines them instead of scrapping the 60-70% unused metal.
why: Cuts primary Ta/W/Ti demand per target 2-3x and shortens lead times; the equipment fits a small machine shop.

title: Gen-8.5 display fabs print gain-cell memory on meter-scale glass
idea: Scale jump from the 300 mm wafer to 2.2 x 2.5 m glass: idle LCD/OLED backplane lines build 2T oxide-TFT gain cells (indium-free ZnSnO or IGZO) at 1.5 um rules. That gives ~3 GB per m2, or ~15 GB per sheet, diced into modules behind an SRAM/DRAM cache.
why: Uses oversupplied existing display capacity with no EUV, no buried tungsten and no HPQ crucibles. At ~$300-600 per sheet, raw cost is ~$20-40/GB, and ~100 ns-1 us latency makes it a far tier.

title: Cold-trap recapture and re-purification of unreacted ALD precursors
idea: Box [any | any | any | any | any | ALD]: insert a condensation trap plus sorbent bed between each ALD chamber and pump to capture the Zr/Hf/Ti amide and Al alkyl precursor that passes unreacted, then redistill it centrally and requalify it by NMR and ICP-MS.
why: Hf/Zr/Ti precursor and energy intensity: ALD precursor utilization is often <10%, so recapture could cut precursor purchases ~5x for the high-k steps that dominate DRAM ALD.

title: Stepwise adiabatic wordline charging recycles the 3-volt swing
idea: Time-stretch the ns wordline edge into 4-8 small voltage steps fed from on-die tank capacitors held at intermediate levels. When the wordline closes, charge flows back into the tanks, recovering ~60-75% of the CV2 energy for a ~1-2 ns penalty.
why: Attacks the voltage-floor energy: ~3x lower wordline energy and smaller VPP charge pumps, so less periphery area and less power drawn per bit.

title: Water-developable chitosan photoresist with zero PFAS
idea: Within $1M/24 months: formulate a chitosan- or cellulose-derived resist with non-fluorinated sulfonium photoacid generators that develops in plain water, and characterize resolution and line-edge roughness on a university e-beam writer and 248 nm scanner.
why: PFAS photoacid generators and solvents face EU and U.S. restrictions; a water-developed bio-resist removes both and cuts solvent waste.

title: Eliminate regulator losses: series-stacked bank domains recycle bitline charge
idea: Stack four bank groups in series across 4x0.5 V rails so charge dumped from one bank's bitlines flows down to power the next domain instead of to ground, with a small switched-capacitor balancer absorbing load mismatch.
why: Charge is reused ~3-4 times and pump/LDO losses (~2.5x) vanish, together ~10x lower energy per activation.

title: Abatement fluoride captured as synthetic fluorspar for HF regeneration
idea: TRIZ #34 Discarding and recovering: run fluorine-bearing scrubber effluent through lime crystallizers that precipitate high-purity CaF2 pellets instead of sludge. The pellets go back to an acid plant that regenerates electronic-grade HF with H2SO4, closing the fab's fluorine loop.
why: Fluorspar is China-dominated (~60%). Recovering ~50-70% of fab fluorine cuts that dependence and sludge disposal, using only Ca, F, S, H and O.

title: Car platform sharing: one die ships as DDR5, LPDDR5X or HBM
idea: Automakers build many models on one platform. Design one array die with dual pad rings, TSV-ready keep-outs and fuse/metal-option selection so the same wafer becomes standard DDR5, LPDDR5X or HBM core dies at test or stacking time, each meeting its unchanged JEDEC interface.
why: Cuts mask sets (several million dollars each, including 5-7 EUV masks) and lets fabs swing wafers to whichever product is short in weeks rather than quarters, raising effective supply ~5-10%.

title: Bread slicer: laser-slice HBM backgrind silicon into reusable wafers
idea: Stimulus 'bread slicer' -> before HBM core dies are thinned to ~50 um, focus an IR laser ~100 um below the device side to write a subsurface cleave plane (stealth-slicing style), lift off the ~650 um remainder intact, polish it and recycle it as a reclaim or donor wafer instead of grinding it to dust.
why: ~90% of each HBM wafer's silicon is ground away; recovering it cuts Cz pulls, crucibles and polysilicon per HBM bit by ~40-50%.

title: Deuterated nitride supporter doubles as an interface-passivation reservoir
idea: Combine the capacitor's existing SiN support lattice with trap passivation (zero added masks): deposit it from SiD4/ND3 so it stores ~20 at.% deuterium, which diffuses down during later anneals and passivates access-transistor interface/GIDL traps with stronger Si-D bonds.
why: Trims the <=13 fA leakage tail that sets refresh; halving it doubles the refresh interval (~23 fJ/bit saved, 5-10% bandwidth back) and replaces high-pressure H2/D2 anneals.

title: Old TV: recycled LCD glass becomes low-CTE package cores
idea: Stimulus 'old TV' (millions of discarded LCD panels) -> LCD panel glass is already alkali-free aluminoborosilicate with CTE ~3.2 ppm/K; strip, re-melt and re-draw it into glass-core substrates and interposers for DRAM/HBM packages with laser-drilled through-glass vias.
why: Replaces single-supplier low-CTE T-glass cloth and reduces ABF dependence from an abundant waste stream; glass cores also allow finer HBM redistribution.

title: Cryogenic CO2-argon aerosol cleaning replaces wet rinse steps
idea: TRIZ #36 Phase transitions: replace selected post-CMP and pre-deposition wet-clean, rinse and dry steps with a cryogenic aerosol of solid CO2/Ar micro-crystals. The crystals knock particles off by momentum transfer and then sublime, leaving no liquid or residue.
why: Cuts UPW and IPA per wafer pass (~10-20% of fab UPW in the targeted steps) and removes capillary forces that collapse 60-75:1 capacitor pillars.

title: Eliminate the memory package: oxide memory built in the logic die's BEOL
idea: Deposit 4-8 tiers of indium/gallium-free oxide 2T0C cells in the upper metal stack of the accelerator die itself at <=400 C, wired by vias a few microns from the compute that uses them.
why: Removes the PHY, TSVs, interposer, separate wafer and package; access energy falls from 3-4 pJ/bit (HBM) to ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit.

title: MgB2 superconducting flux-loop memory at 20 K, helium-free
idea: Periodic-table walk, Mg (12): build persistent-current flux-quantum cells with MgB2 (Tc 39 K) junctions and kinetic inductors, operated at 20 K by cryocooler or liquid H2 instead of liquid He, as a zero-static-power working memory in cryogenic AI pods.
why: Zero refresh, near-zero energy per bit; avoids Nb (~85% Brazil) and He (Qatar); Mg and B are abundant.

title: Maskless four-beam interference lithography for periodic DRAM cell arrays
idea: Box [honeycomb cap array | buried WL | voltage SA | standard | Si | immersion four-beam interference from a 266 nm solid-state laser + spacer doubling]: because the cell array is perfectly periodic, expose its holes and gratings with interfering beams (~46 nm half-pitch, no mask, no projection lens), halve the pitch with spacers, and trim array edges with a coarse LED block exposure.
why: Removes rare-gas light sources and masks for ~5 array layers; an interference tool costs maybe 1/20 of an EUV scanner.

title: R744 car-AC playbook: CO2 replaces Fluorinert in chuck chillers
idea: Automakers moved air conditioning from fluorinated refrigerants to transcritical CO2 (R744); do the same for etch and CVD chuck temperature control by running direct-expansion CO2 microchannels inside the chuck base instead of pumping perfluorinated heat-transfer fluid from separate chillers.
why: 3M ended PFAS fluid production in 2025, stranding Fluorinert/Galden-type chillers; CO2 is non-PFAS and nearly free, and direct expansion removes the secondary loop, cutting chiller energy ~20-30% and enabling -40 C cryo-etch chucks.

title: Po memory never forgets because it is cold: 77 K planar cells
idea: Po: 'memory that never forgets.' Extracted: run 180 nm-built DRAM in liquid nitrogen, where junction and subthreshold leakage fall by many orders of magnitude, so a simple planar MOS capacitor of 3-5 fF holds data for hours and refresh nearly vanishes; LN2 comes from air, not helium.
why: Lets cheap planar 180 nm cells (no high-AR etch, no high-k) work; refresh energy ~0 and transistors get faster; the price is ~10 W of wall power per W removed at 77 K, best in already-cooled racks.

title: Reopen U.S. 200 mm fabs for Grade-1 automotive DRAM
idea: Magnify the node on purpose: run 65-90 nm DRAM with fat capacitors and long, low-leakage access transistors in idle U.S. 200 mm fabs, qualified to AEC-Q100 Grade 1 (125 C), with DUV only.
why: Cars need 2-16 GB each of hot-rated DRAM. Moving that volume off leading-edge lines frees EUV wafers for HBM and adds U.S. supply with no EUV and little helium.

title: Eliminate writability for frozen weights: via-programmed 3D ROM replaces DRAM
idea: Encode a deployed model's weights as present/absent vias in 4-8 stacked metal layers written by maskless e-beam on mature-node wafers, read by low-swing sensing with no refresh or capacitor, with only activations kept in DRAM.
why: Weights are ~50% of inference memory; ROM reads at ~0.05 pJ/bit with zero refresh and frees DRAM supply, using no EUV or high-AR capacitor.

title: Superconformal electroplated copper wordline tiers replace tungsten in 3D stacks
idea: Tungsten replacement gates in 3D stacks need ~25-30 nm tiers for acceptable resistance; Cu's resistivity is ~3x lower, so bottom-up electroplating with suppressor/accelerator additives fills ~12 nm tier cavities through the slit, using a ~1 nm self-forming MnSiO3 barrier.
why: Tier pitch down ~35%, so ~1.5x more tiers per etchable height; with a 120-tier gain-cell stack that is ~10x at equal cost, with no tungsten (China ~80%) or WF6.

title: Historian revives Sandia's protonic memory in plain silicon dioxide
idea: Persona: a historian of forgotten technology recalling Sandia's 1990s work. A hydrogen anneal puts mobile protons into an ultrathin buried SiO2 layer. A gate field parks them at the top or bottom interface, which shifts the transistor threshold and holds it without power.
why: Non-volatile 1T memory from Si, O and H only, entirely native to a CMOS fab. Risk: write speed.

title: Band-to-band tunneling access transistors flatten the retention leakage tail
idea: Effect: quantum band-to-band tunneling. Replace the thermionic access FET with an all-silicon tunnel FET whose off-state leakage is set by tunneling, giving aA/um levels that barely depend on temperature. The weak-cell tail vanishes, and the low on-current is fine because charging 5 fF at 1 uA takes only ~5 ns.
why: Access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3): refresh intervals 10-100x longer cut refresh energy and bandwidth loss; Si-only, with no Ge or III-V.

title: Rutile titania on MoO2 electrodes: hafnium- and zirconium-free capacitors
idea: Imposed scarcity: zero Zr and Hf. Use conductive MoO2 (a distorted-rutile oxide) as the storage-node electrode so ALD TiO2 grows directly as rutile (k ~80-100) at low temperature, with Al doping to hold down leakage in the thin film.
why: k~90 vs ZAZ ~40 lets the cell reach 5 fF at roughly half the aspect ratio, easing etch and leaning; uses abundant Ti and domestic Mo instead of nuclear-chain Zr/Hf precursors or PGM Ru electrodes.

title: Scarce-input substitution credits verified by digital material passports
idea: Ideal: a market that rewards memory made from nothing scarce. Closest: a U.S. per-GB production credit scaled by the share of the bill of materials free of designated chokepoints (helium, natural HPQ, Chinese-origin W/Ge/Ga/In, PFAS), verified with lot-level material passports (supplier attestations plus isotopic/trace fingerprints).
why: Creates demand pull for He-, W-, HPQ- and PFAS-free processes, pulling their time-to-volume in by years and shifting adoption risk from fabs to policy.
